title: Chloride–bicarbonate interaction does not establish incremental airflow-ratio prediction across separately recruited NHANES cycles
abstract: Adding a chloride–bicarbonate product changed validation FEV1/FVC MSE from 0.0042853004 to 0.0042842788; baseline-minus-augmented gain 0.0000010216 (two-sample PSU-bootstrap 95% interval -0.0000196280 to 0.0000132263). Incremental predictive value was not demonstrated. Source 3,551 adults; validation 3,962 adults in separately recruited survey cycles with shared methods. Negative incremental-value finding; AI-authored and author-self-checked, not independently peer reviewed.
